items.summary: For the first time in history, three Black women will serve simultaneously in the U.S. Senate when Illinois Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton takes office in January. Why it matters: It took over 235 years for two Black women to serve in the U.S. Senate at the same time. Two years later, that number will grow to three. Driving the news: Stratton won election to the U.S. Senate on Tuesday, defeating Republican Don Tracy, per AP. She'll join Sens. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Delaware) and Angela Alsobrooks (D-Maryland), who were both elected in 2024 and became the first two Black women to serve simultaneously in 2025. The Stratton campaign did not immediately respond to Axios' request for comment. Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response
items.summary: A new study suggests that ultra-processed foods may influence children's developing brains in ways that encourage weight gain. Researchers from USC studied 46 children ages 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods like cookies and French fries. These heightened brain responses were linked to greater increases in body fat and body mass index (BMI) one year later, suggesting that the brain's sensitivity to food cues may help explain why ultra-processed diets are associated with obesity.

Joey Logano says his team tried to hand him the championship at Martinsville, but pit crew errors cost him a shot at the 2026 title. The race at Martinsville Speedway was supposed to be a comeback story for Logano. He had climbed to fifth in the standings after a slow start to the season. A win or a strong finish on Sunday could have kept his championship hopes alive until the final race. Instead, the car ended up stuck on pit road while the leaders pulled away. Logano admitted the team had the race under control before the errors happened. He said they were in a spot they liked until things went wrong. The first issue forced an extra stop under green flags to tighten a loose wheel. The…

Dylan Larkin's suspension forced Detroit to find a new top-line center and a new voice. #RedWings Regardless of how you feel about Dylan Larkin and the situation surrounding him, he is an amazing player and a first-line center. Provisional Met Office figures just released show the UK had a warmer, wetter and sunnier October than average but quieter weather has now arrived. High pressure has seized control of the UK weather meaning largely dry, settled but chilly autumn conditions will continue this week. Days will bring a mix of patchy cloud, sunny spells and a few showers, with frost and fog expected to form at night - especially in northern and western areas. A federal judge on Friday rejected McDonald’s request to dismiss a proposed class action accusing it of defrauding consumers about the content of its McRib sandwich. The plaintiffs accused McDonald’s of intentionally shaping McRib patties with ridges to resemble pork ribs and make diners believe the sandwich contains rib meat, an expensive cut known for its higher fat content and rich flavor. Consumers said McDonald’s actual use of lower-grade pork products including shoulder, heart, tripe or stomach caused them to overpay for the McRib, one of its most expensive menu items.

Rarely does a delay of game penalty actually help the team with the ball, but it did on Monday night. They say "when it rains, it pours," but it's the opposite for the Bears right now. The Indiana Pacers had just six players available for Monday’s 108-104 home loss to the Atlanta Hawks. Injuries and rest kept Tyrese Haliburton and 10 teammates out on the second night of a back-to-back. The bare-bones group took the floor just eight games into a season that many expected to be a bounce-back year for Haliburton and Co. Fans quickly questioned how a team could be this depleted so early on, while one called for refunds for those in attendance. Indiana's six available players were earning about $15 million combined this season, according to The Associated Press, while roughly $193 million in salary sat out. No Pacers team had gone with so few players since 2004.

It's been three years since Broncos kicker Wil Lutz missed an extra point. After hitting both his extra points in Sunday's win over the Chiefs, Lutz has now made 113 consecutive extra points without a miss. That's the longest streak in the NFL since the 2015 rule change that moved extra points back by 13 yards. The previous record of 112 consecutive extra points was set by Justin Tucker with the Ravens. "I've [said] a hundred times how much I value the extra point . I value them a lot. But my goal isn't to break the record, it's to make every one the rest of the season, so whatever that number is at the end of the season," Lutz told Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette .

ROME (AP) — Next year’s Giro d’Italia will start in Trieste, cross briefly into Slovenia, and climb up three iconic mountains in the final week before the mostly ceremonial finish in Rome.The route for the 110th Giro, scheduled for May 8-30, was presented in Rome on Monday. The 21 stages will be made up of: two time trials, six sprint stages, eight medium mountain legs and five in the high mountains on a total route of 3,418.9 kilometers (2,124.4 miles). The Giro will open with a 172-kilometer stage that starts and finishes in Trieste, crossing the nearby border briefly into Slovenia. The second stage is entirely in Slovenia before crossing back into Italy for the rest of the race.

Is that water in your spacecraft, or are you just happy to see the delta-V. The brothers launched rockets, refurbished rockets, and sold rockets. But when it came time for them to leave SpaceX and start their own space company—a lifetime dream for the Carlisle brothers—they chose not to build rockets. Rather, they focused on spacecraft. In late 2022, the three Carlisles founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. They chose water, which is potentially harvestable on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, as a means of propulsion.

The 1972 Miami Dolphins celebrated this weekend after the previously-undefeated Vikings lost, but one member of the historic team passed away. According to an obituary published on Legacy, former Dolphins defensive lineman Bob Heinz died on Saturday at 79 years old. Heinz played collegiately at Delta College and the University of the Pacific before the Dolphins took him in the second round (No. 37 overall) of the 1969 NFL Draft. He spent nine seasons with Miami, appearing in 111 games and recording nine sacks. The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner. New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial. The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer. Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations. More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.

MLB is facing a lockout on December 1st as they continue to push a salary cap system. Today they offered up to push the cap system out to 2028, along with other changes. The league's transition proposal to the MLB Players Association delays salary cap and floor implementation to 2028 for a smoother transition, with a projected cap of $180.2 million and a floor of $150 million. Other key reforms proposed include raising minimum salaries, reducing roster churn, eliminating draft pick compensation, and expanding free-agent access. The plan aims to balance team competitiveness, player benefits, and market stability.
